Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble? 23 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Liv McMahon , Technology reporter and Osmond Chia , Business reporter How did AI discover the internet's massive cyber-security risk? For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet. It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert. Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side programming language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks. Governments and cyber-security agencies rushed to contain the fallout , urging website owners to check if their sites were affected and, if so, install updates to patch the issue or consider going offline. There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far. But in the days since the issues came to light, disruption to sites and services has continued to ripple around the world. What is PHP? Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily. It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server. The award, often considered the second most prestigious award in the physical sciences, after the Nobel Prize in Physics, cited Ye’s achievement in “transformative, widely applicable advances in the control of ultracold atomic systems.” Ye, a physicist at JILA, a joint institute of NIST and the University of Colorado Boulder, shares the prize with Immanuel Bloch, the scientific director at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics in Garching, Germany. pages.text: Pirates’ best players not in the Hall of Fame Skip to Content PITTSBURGH -- The Pirates’ greatest players have a place in Cooperstown. Honus Wagner was part of the Hall of Fame’s first class. The Hall waived its mandatory five-year waiting period to elect Roberto Clemente in 1973, less than a year after his tragic death. Willie Stargell , Paul Waner , Arky Vaughan , Bill Mazeroski , Pie Traynor , Max Carey , Fred Clarke , Ralph Kiner -- they all achieved baseball immortality by being inducted into the Hall of Fame. • Hall of Fame coverage But not all the best players to take the field in Pittsburgh have received that recognition, even with Dave Parker finally making the Hall in the Class of 2025 . There are Hall of Fame “snubs” -- players who deserved (or still deserve) to be inducted but were simply overlooked. And there are others who had careers worth remembering, even if their credentials don’t quite compare to their Hall of Fame peers. Here, we’ll take a look at five of the Pirates’ best players you won’t find represented in Cooperstown. The National Monument includes the A.G. Gaston Motel, which served as the headquarters for the Birmingham campaign. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Canyons of the Ancients National Monument | Colorado View Map In Full Screen Canyons of the Ancients National Monument, located in the Four Corners region of southwestern Colorado, protects a stunning cultural landscape with the highest known density of archaeological sites in the United States. Encompassing 176,000 acres of public lands, the Monument features more than 8,300 documented sites—including villages, kivas, field houses, cliff dwellings, petroglyphs, and ancient roadways—with estimates suggesting over 30,000 yet to be recorded. These sites offer a window into over 12,000 years of human history, primarily shaped by Ancestral Puebloan cultures and their descendants. The area continues to be a living landscape used today for traditional purposes, recreation, hunting, livestock grazing, and energy development. It also encompasses Cross Canyon , Sego Lily, and Cahone Canyon Wilderness Study Areas. While exploring the Monument’s canyons, mesas, and desert terrain, visitors are reminded to Visit with Respect and Leave No Trace to protect the resources that define this unique place. View cultural sites : Visit mesa‑top pueblos and petroglyph panels. Look, photograph, and leave artifacts in place. Featured sites include: Badger Springs Trailhead : Short route down Badger Springs Wash to the Agua Fria River and a petroglyph panel at the confluence. Pueblo La Plata Cultural Site : A large mesa‑top village reachable by high‑clearance road, followed by a rocky walk. pages.text: Players Who Hit For the Cycle Skip to Content Getting four knocks in one day is memorable for even the best hitters. But getting a hit of each kind -- a single, double, triple and homer -- in the same game? That's something special. How special? It's only happened once in postseason history, when the Red Sox's Brock Holt achieved the feat against the Yankees in the 2018 American League Division Series. It's a rare enough occurrence that it took the Marlins 30 years to notch their first cycle, and they still have as many World Series championships as a franchise as players who have hit for the cycle. pages.text: Polar Bears in the Roman Colosseum? | National Geographic By Candida Moss Published September 28, 2026 Want to make sure you get every Stones & Bones newsletter? Put your email here . There’s a strange and intriguing reference in the writings of a first-century Roman poet who describes a showdown between bears and seals (or, as he called them, “sea-calves”) in the Colosseum. Only polar bears are known to fight seals, so this raises a question no modern scholar has yet been able to answer: How on Earth would arctic bears have traveled to the heart of the Roman Empire? A clue to the ursine mystery has recently emerged—in the first English language book on Scandinavian Roman-era history, Dagfinn Skre's The Northern Routes to Kingshi p . Skre places Sweden, Norway, and Denmark at the periphery of the empire, showing that Denmark was only a four-week march from the Roman frontier. And in fact, the Roman military was recruiting from the region by the late first century A.D. So the social networks and infrastructure were in place to facilitate the movement of exotic animals that Rome craved for its spectacles. I reached out to Michael Kulikowski, a professor of classics at Penn State who wrote about Skre’s work for the London Review of Books , for more on how polar bears could have ended up on the sands of Rome’s most famous arena. The intellectual property that results from this research and development has the potential to make an impact, but requires translating the scientific discovery into a developed product. This translational work is usually performed by individuals and organizations outside of the government that must devote time and capital to develop the discovery into a successful commercial product. Despite the critical importance of federal R&D to economic development, agencies historically have lacked the resources and interagency platforms to act together in the commercialization of their technologies.
